title: Reachable computation with register-position constraints
statement: Let $P$ be a register program, let an oracle assign Boolean answers to each decider and Boolean-list input, and let $c_0,c_1,c$ be configurations on input $x$. For a register $r$ and integer position $p$, there must be a time $T$ such that the run from $c_0$ at time $T$ equals $c_1$. At every earlier time $t<T$, the run must be in a configuration of the specified form determined by $c$, some state and input-head position, $r$, and $p$, and that state must not be a call node.
hypotheses_covered: An oracle from Fin d to Boolean lists
Configurations c₀, c₁, and c on input x
Existence of a time T at which the run from c₀ equals c₁
At every time t<T, existence of a state and input-head position yielding the specified run configuration, with that state not a call node
caveat: The supplied snippet does not define rrun or xCfg, so the exact meaning of the specified intermediate configuration form is unavailable.
